specification.problem: Trotterized time evolution of a second-quantized molecular Hamiltonian under Jordan-Wigner, with Hartree-Fock or fixed-particle-number state preparation, and classical estimation of Trotter error and step count restricted to the eta-electron subspace.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: H2 in a minimal basis (n=4 spin orbitals, eta=2), second-order Trotter, statevector simulation, no ancilla. Compare ground-state energy error of the Trotter unitary against r. Excluded: phase estimation/Hadamard test, the paper's actual error bounds, Z and filling-fraction scaling analysis, and larger molecules. Integrals h_pq and h_pqrs must be supplied externally.

symbols.meaning: Pauli-string terms of H after Jordan-Wigner, with coefficients absorbed

equations.label: Second-quantized Hamiltonian
equations.description: Electronic Hamiltonian, decomposed into Pauli strings via Jordan-Wigner.
equations.justification: Standard quantum chemistry form; the abstract only mentions quantum chemistry simulation.

equations.label: Second-order product formula
equations.description: Symmetric second-order Trotter-Suzuki evolution; each Pauli exponential is a CNOT ladder, RZ, and the reverse ladder.
equations.justification: The abstract refers to Trotterization; the order is chosen per the sketch default.

equations.label: Hartree-Fock state
equations.description: Slater determinant under Jordan-Wigner, with qubit p set to 1 if orbital p is occupied (qubit 0 is the least-significant bit).
equations.justification: Standard JW preparation; it stands in for the paper's improved state preparation, which is not specified.
assumptions: occupied set known, e.g. orbitals 0 and 1 for H2

equations.label: Effective Hamiltonian error in subspace
equations.latex: \epsilon(r)=\left|\langle\psi_0|\tilde H_r|\psi_0\rangle-E_0\right|,\quad U_r=e^{-i\tilde H_r t},\ \epsilon\sim C\,(t/r)^2\ \text{for second order}
equations.description: Ground-state error from the Trotter unitary, where tilde H_r is the effective Hamiltonian, computed in the eta-electron subspace via Pi_eta. The scaling constant C is fitted numerically.
equations.abstract_quote: numerical results for small systems fail to reveal any clear correlation between ground state error and number of spin orbitals
equations.justification: The abstract discusses ground-state error from Trotterization; the (t/r)^2 form is standard background for second-order formulas, and C is not given.
assumptions: error measured in the fixed-particle subspace
t/r small enough for the asymptotic regime

equations.label: Step count from classical extrapolation
equations.description: Choose r from the error measured at several small step sizes, without extra quantum resources.
equations.abstract_quote: to use classical processing to further reduce the required Trotter step size and to estimate the necessary number of steps, without requiring additional quantum resources
equations.justification: This is one concrete reading of the classical estimation strategy; the paper's actual method is unknown.
assumptions: second-order scaling holds at the sampled r_k

registers.name: q
registers.role: JW spin-orbital qubits; qubit i is orbital i

specification.initial_state: HF determinant with X on the occupied qubits (eq_3).

steps.description: Load or compute the H2 integrals, build the JW Pauli terms, and verify with exact diagonalization in the eta=2 sector for E_0 and psi_0.
Prepare the HF state with X gates.
Build U_r with Pauli-exponential gadgets (or PauliEvolutionGate with SuzukiTrotter order 2) for several r.
Classically compute the effective-Hamiltonian ground-state error restricted to the eta-electron subspace for several r, fit C, and choose r.

specification.measurement: Statevector simulation with no measurements: read the energy expectation or the overlap with the exact ground state.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Restrict to the eta-electron subspace, fit epsilon versus (t/r)^2, and choose r from eq_5.
assumptions: H2, minimal basis, n=4, eta=2, no ancilla
missing_information: the paper's actual error bounds and commutator expressions
how Z and eta/n enter quantitatively
the improved state preparation circuit details (Givens ladder angles)
